questions.title: Sequential Ticket Generator
questions.objective: Print N zero-padded ticket numbers TICK-001 to TICK-N using range().
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A ticket system must print N ticket numbers in order. Every ticket starts with TICK- followed by the ticket number padded with zeros to 3 digits.
• Ticket 1 → TICK-001
• Ticket 12 → TICK-012
• Ticket 100 → TICK-100

Given N, print the tickets from TICK-001 up to TICK-N, one per line. Use a for loop with range().
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
questions.output_format: N lines. Line i contains: TICK-<i padded with zeros to 3 digits>
sample_outputs:
TICK-001
TICK-002
TICK-003
TICK-004
TICK-005
TICK-006
TICK-007
TICK-008
TICK-009
TICK-010
TICK-011
TICK-012
hints: range(1, N + 1) gives the numbers 1 to N.
Zero-padding to 3 digits can be done with the format specifier :03d.
Inside the loop print f"TICK-{i:03d}".

questions.title: Cumulative Streak Points
questions.objective: Compute prefix sum of points earned over N days (Day i earns i points).
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A game gives a player points every day, and the points equal the day number: Day 1 earns 1 point, Day 2 earns 2 points, and so on.
• The running total after a day = all points earned from Day 1 up to that day
• Example: after Day 3 the total is 1 + 2 + 3 = 6

Given N days, print one line for each day showing the running total after that day.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer N (number of days).
questions.output_format: N lines. Line i: Day i: <total points after day i>
hints: Keep a variable total that starts at 0.
In each iteration i of range(1, N + 1), add i to total.
Print the day number and the total inside the loop.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
total = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    total += i
    print(f"Day {i}: {total}")

questions.title: Quantity Price Schedule
questions.objective: Print 20-row unit price schedule for units 1 to 20 with aligned columns.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A shop prints a price table for buying 1 to 20 units of an item. The price for u units is u x price_per_unit.
• First print a header line: the word Units right-aligned in 5 characters, followed by the word Total right-aligned in 10 characters
• Then print 20 rows, one for each u from 1 to 20: u right-aligned in 5 characters, followed by the total price right-aligned in 10 characters
• Do not print anything between the columns or after the last column

Example for price_per_unit = 10 (first lines):
Units Total
1 10
2 20

Given the price per unit, print the full table.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer: price_per_unit.
questions.output_format: 21 lines. Line 1 is the header (Units right-aligned in width 5, Total right-aligned in width 10). Then 20 rows: u right-aligned in width 5, followed by u * price_per_unit right-aligned in width 10.
hints: The total price for u units is u * price_per_unit.
In an f-string, {value:>5} right-aligns the value in a field of 5 characters.
Print the header with the same widths first, then loop u over range(1, 21).
questions.reference_solution:
p = int(input())
print(f"{'Units':>5}{'Total':>10}")
for u in range(1, 21):
    print(f"{u:>5}{u * p:>10}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer: price_per_unit.

questions.title: Integer Digit Counter
questions.objective: Count number of digits in an integer using division by 10 in a while loop.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Count how many digits an integer has by repeatedly dividing it by 10 inside a while loop.
• Each division by 10 (n // 10) removes the last digit
• Count the divisions until the number becomes 0
• The number 0 has 1 digit
• For a negative number, ignore the minus sign (-908 has 3 digits)

Example: 12345 has 5 digits. Given n, print the number of digits.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
questions.output_format: One line: Digits: <count>
hints: Use abs(n) so that negative numbers work.
The number 0 still has one digit, so count at least once before checking n == 0.
Each loop step: n //= 10 and count += 1.
questions.reference_solution:
n = abs(int(input()))
count = 0
while True:
    n //= 10
    count += 1
    if n == 0:
        break
print(f"Digits: {count}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Digits: <count>

questions.title: Sum of Digits Accumulator
questions.objective: Accumulate sum of digits of non-negative integer using modulo and division.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Find the sum of all digits of a non-negative integer using % and //.
• n % 10 gives the last digit
• n // 10 removes the last digit
• Repeat until n becomes 0 and add every digit to a total

Example: 1234 → 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10. For 0 the sum is 0.

Given n, print the sum of its digits.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one non-negative integer n.
questions.output_format: One line: Digit sum: <sum>
hints: Start with total = 0.
While n > 0: add n % 10 to total, then do n //= 10.
If n is 0 the loop does not run and the answer stays 0.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
total = 0
while n > 0:
    total += n % 10
    n //= 10
print(f"Digit sum: {total}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one non-negative integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Digit sum: <sum>

questions.title: Divisor Enumeration
questions.objective: Find and print all integer divisors of N in ascending order.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A divisor of N is a number that divides N with no remainder.
• Check every number from 1 to N
• Keep the numbers i where N % i == 0
• Print them from smallest to largest in one line, separated by single spaces

Example: the divisors of 12 are 1 2 3 4 6 12. The number 1 has only one divisor, which is 1.

Given N, print all its divisors.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
questions.output_format: One line: Divisors: <d1> <d2> ... (space-separated, in ascending order)
hints: Loop i from 1 to N using range(1, N + 1).
i is a divisor when N % i == 0.
Collect the divisors in a list and print them with ' '.join(...).

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Divisors: <d1> <d2> ... (space-separated, in ascending order)

questions.title: Right-Angle Star Triangle
questions.objective: Print N-row triangle where row i contains i # symbols.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Print a right-angle triangle made of # symbols with N rows.

• Row 2 has 2 #
• Row i has i # (no spaces between them)
• The last row has N #

Example for N = 4:
#
##
###
####

Given N, print the triangle.

hints: Use for i in range(1, N + 1) to go through the rows.
A row with i hashes is the string '#' * i.

questions.title: Sentinel Input Accumulator
questions.objective: Read integers until sentinel -1; output sum and count of valid numbers.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A program reads numbers, one per line, until it sees the special value -1. This value is called a sentinel: it means "stop reading" and it is not part of the data.
• Every number before -1 is a valid number
• Add up the valid numbers and count them
• If -1 is the very first value, the sum is 0 and the count is 0

Example: input 10, 20, 30, -1 → sum is 60 and count is 3.

Use a while loop to read the numbers, then print the sum and the count.
questions.input_format: Several lines, each containing one integer. The last line is -1 (the sentinel).
questions.output_format:
Two lines:
Line 1: Sum: <sum of valid numbers>
Line 2: Count: <how many valid numbers>
questions.constraints:
Every valid number satisfies 0 <= number <= 10^9
-1 appears exactly once, as the last line
At most 1000 valid numbers
hints: Use while True to read one number each time with int(input()).
When the number is -1, break out of the loop without adding it.
Keep two variables, total and count, both starting at 0.
questions.reference_solution:
total = 0
count = 0
while True:
    x = int(input())
    if x == -1:
        break
    total += x
    count += 1
print(f"Sum: {total}")
print(f"Count: {count}")

extra_fields.input_format: Several lines, each containing one integer. The last line is -1 (the sentinel).
extra_fields.output_format:
Two lines:
Line 1: Sum: <sum of valid numbers>
Line 2: Count: <how many valid numbers>

questions.title: Integer Reverse via Modulo
questions.objective: Reverse integer mathematically using while loop without string conversion.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Reverse the digits of an integer using only math. Do not use str(), slicing or any string conversion.
• n % 10 gives the last digit
• reversed = reversed * 10 + last digit builds the new number
• n // 10 removes the last digit
• Zeros at the end of the original number disappear after reversing (1200 → 21)
• A negative number keeps its minus sign (-908 → -809)
• 0 reversed is 0

Given n, print the reversed number.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
questions.output_format: One line: Reversed: <reversed number>
hints: Remember whether n is negative, then work with abs(n).
In the loop: rev = rev * 10 + n % 10, then n //= 10.
Put the minus sign back at the end if the original number was negative.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
neg = n < 0
n = abs(n)
rev = 0
while n > 0:
    rev = rev * 10 + n % 10
    n //= 10
print(f"Reversed: {-rev if neg else rev}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Reversed: <reversed number>

questions.title: Even & Odd Digit Segregator
questions.objective: Count even and odd digits in an integer using single loop traversal.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Count how many digits of an integer are even and how many are odd. Use one loop that goes through the digits only once.
• Take each digit with n % 10 and remove it with n // 10
• A digit is even if digit % 2 == 0, otherwise it is odd
• 0 is an even digit, and the number 0 has exactly one digit (which is even)
• For a negative number, ignore the minus sign

Example: 123456 has 3 even digits (2, 4, 6) and 3 odd digits (1, 3, 5).

Given n, print the count of even digits and the count of odd digits.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
questions.output_format:
Two lines:
Line 1: Even digits: <count>
Line 2: Odd digits: <count>
hints: Use abs(n) so negative numbers work.
Take the last digit with d = n % 10 and test d % 2 == 0.
Handle n = 0 by checking the digit first and testing n == 0 after removing it (do-while style loop).
questions.reference_solution:
n = abs(int(input()))
even = 0
odd = 0
while True:
    d = n % 10
    if d % 2 == 0:
        even += 1
    else:
        odd += 1
    n //= 10
    if n == 0:
        break
print(f"Even digits: {even}")
print(f"Odd digits: {odd}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
extra_fields.output_format:
Two lines:
Line 1: Even digits: <count>
Line 2: Odd digits: <count>

questions.title: Prime Number Verification
questions.objective: Check primality of N in O(sqrt(N)) time using trial division with early break.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A prime number is greater than 1 and has no divisors other than 1 and itself. To check quickly whether N is prime, use trial division:
• Numbers less than 2 (including 1) are not prime
• Try dividing N by i = 2, 3, 4, ... while i * i <= N (you only need to go up to the square root of N)
• Stop at once with break as soon as some i divides N (early break)
• If no i divides N, then N is prime

Example: 91 = 7 × 13, so 91 is not prime.

Given N, print whether it is PRIME or NOT PRIME.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
questions.output_format: One line: Result: <PRIME/NOT PRIME>
hints: If N < 2, the answer is NOT PRIME right away.
Loop i from 2 while i * i <= N (a while loop is the simplest).
If N % i == 0, mark N as not prime and break.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
is_prime = n >= 2
i = 2
while i * i <= n:
    if n % i == 0:
        is_prime = False
        break
    i += 1
print("Result: PRIME" if is_prime else "Result: NOT PRIME")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Result: <PRIME/NOT PRIME>

questions.title: Prime Enumeration in Range
questions.objective: Print all prime numbers between two integers A and B inclusive.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Print all prime numbers from A to B, including A and B. A prime number is greater than 1 and is divisible only by 1 and itself.
• Go through every number from A to B
• For each number, test primality by trial division up to its square root
• Print the primes in increasing order on one line, separated by single spaces
• If there is no prime in the range, print a message saying so
• Remember that 1 is not a prime number

Example: A = 10, B = 30 → 11 13 17 19 23 29.

Given A and B, print all primes in the range.
questions.input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers A and B.
questions.output_format:
If primes exist, one line: Primes: <p1> <p2> ... (space-separated)
If there is none, one line: No primes found
hints: Numbers below 2 are never prime.
Use an outer loop over A..B and an inner loop that tries divisors while i * i <= number.
Collect the primes in a list; if the list is empty print the message instead.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers A and B.
extra_fields.output_format:
If primes exist, one line: Primes: <p1> <p2> ... (space-separated)
If there is none, one line: No primes found

questions.title: Fibonacci Sequence Generator
questions.objective: Generate first N terms of Fibonacci sequence using a, b = b, a + b.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: The Fibonacci sequence starts with 0 and 1. Every next term is the sum of the previous two terms: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...
• Keep two variables a and b, starting with a = 0 and b = 1
• Take a as the next term, then update both together: a, b = b, a + b
• Repeat this for N terms

Example: N = 6 → 0 1 1 2 3 5.

Given N, print the first N terms in one line, separated by single spaces.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
questions.output_format: One line: Fibonacci: <t1> <t2> ... <tN> (space-separated)
hints: Start with a, b = 0, 1.
In each iteration, save a as the next term, then do a, b = b, a + b.
Collect the terms in a list and join them with spaces.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
a, b = 0, 1
terms = []
for _ in range(n):
    terms.append(str(a))
    a, b = b, a + b
print("Fibonacci: " + " ".join(terms))

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Fibonacci: <t1> <t2> ... <tN> (space-separated)

questions.title: Euclidean Greatest Common Divisor
questions.objective: Compute GCD of two integers using Euclid's subtraction/modulo loop with step logging.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: The GCD (greatest common divisor) of two numbers is the largest number that divides both of them. Euclid's method finds it with a loop:
• While b is not 0: find r = a % b, then set a = b and b = r
• When b becomes 0, the answer is a
• Print every loop step on its own line, in the format shown in the output format
• If a is smaller than b at the start, the first step just swaps them (a % b = a)

Example: for 48 and 18 the steps are 48 % 18 = 12, 18 % 12 = 6, 12 % 6 = 0. So the GCD is 6.

Given a and b, print every step and then the GCD.
questions.input_format: A single line containing two space-separated positive integers a and b.
questions.output_format:
Several lines:
One line per step: Step <k>: <a> % <b> = <r>   (k starts at 1)
Last line: GCD: <value>
hints: Use a while loop that runs while b != 0.
Inside the loop: r = a % b, print the step with a counter, then a, b = b, r.
After the loop, a holds the GCD.
questions.reference_solution:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
step = 0
while b != 0:
    r = a % b
    step += 1
    print(f"Step {step}: {a} % {b} = {r}")
    a, b = b, r
print(f"GCD: {a}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing two space-separated positive integers a and b.
extra_fields.output_format:
Several lines:
One line per step: Step <k>: <a> % <b> = <r>   (k starts at 1)
Last line: GCD: <value>

questions.title: Numeric Palindrome Checker
questions.objective: Determine whether an integer is palindrome purely through numeric reversal.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A palindrome number reads the same forwards and backwards (for example 121 or 1221). Check this using math only. Do not convert the number to a string.
• Build the reversed number with a while loop: reversed = reversed * 10 + n % 10, then n //= 10
• Compare the reversed number with the original number
• Negative numbers are never palindromes (-121 is NOT a palindrome)
• 0 is a palindrome

Example: 121 reversed is 121, so it is a palindrome. 10 reversed is 1, so it is not.

Given n, print PALINDROME or NOT PALINDROME.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
questions.output_format: One line: Result: <PALINDROME/NOT PALINDROME>
hints: A negative number can be rejected immediately.
Keep a copy of the original number and reverse the other copy.
If reversed == original, the number is a palindrome.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
if n < 0:
    ok = False
else:
    orig = n
    rev = 0
    while n > 0:
        rev = rev * 10 + n % 10
        n //= 10
    ok = rev == orig
print("Result: PALINDROME" if ok else "Result: NOT PALINDROME")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer n.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Result: <PALINDROME/NOT PALINDROME>

questions.title: Binary Exponentiation Loop
questions.objective: Compute base^exp % mod in O(log exp) time using iterative bit-shifting multiplication.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Compute (base ^ exp) % mod quickly. Do not use pow() and do not run a loop exp times (exp can be huge). Use binary exponentiation, which needs only about log2(exp) steps:
• Start with result = 1 % mod and base = base % mod
• While exp > 0: if the last bit of exp is 1 (exp & 1), set result = result * base % mod
• Then square the base (base = base * base % mod) and shift exp right by one bit (exp >>= 1)
• Any number raised to the power 0 is 1, so the answer is 1 % mod in that case

Example: 2 ^ 10 % 1000 = 1024 % 1000 = 24.

Given base, exp and mod, print the result.
questions.input_format: A single line containing three space-separated integers: base, exp and mod.
questions.output_format: One line: Result: <(base ^ exp) % mod>
hints: Starting with result = 1 % mod handles mod = 1 correctly (the answer is 0).
exp & 1 tells you whether the lowest bit of exp is 1.
After every step do base = base * base % mod and exp >>= 1.
questions.reference_solution:
base, exp, mod = map(int, input().split())
result = 1 % mod
base %= mod
while exp > 0:
    if exp & 1:
        result = result * base % mod
    base = base * base % mod
    exp >>= 1
print(f"Result: {result}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing three space-separated integers: base, exp and mod.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Result: <(base ^ exp) % mod>

questions.title: ASCII Diamond Contour
questions.objective: Print an ASCII diamond of size N (odd) using centered # characters and spaces.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Print a hollow diamond (only its outline) of odd size N using # characters and spaces. The diamond has N rows, and the widest row is the middle row.
• The first row and the last row have a single #
• Every other row has two # characters: one on the left edge and one on the right edge of the diamond, with spaces between them
• Leading spaces keep the diamond centered
• Do not print trailing spaces at the end of any row
• N = 1 prints a single #

Example for N = 5:
#
# #
# #
# #
#

Given N, print the diamond.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one odd integer N.
questions.output_format: N lines forming the hollow diamond. No row has trailing spaces.
hints: Let mid = N // 2. Row i has abs(mid - i) leading spaces.
Let k = mid - abs(mid - i). If k == 0 the row is a single #.
Otherwise print # + (2 * k - 1) spaces + #.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one odd integer N.
extra_fields.output_format: N lines forming the hollow diamond. No row has trailing spaces.

questions.title: Collatz Sequence Traversal
questions.objective: Generate Collatz sequence for N, tracking total steps and maximum value reached.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: The Collatz sequence starts from a positive integer N and follows two rules until it reaches 1:
• If the current number is even, the next number is number // 2
• If the current number is odd, the next number is 3 * number + 1
• Each move is one step. The sequence includes N itself and ends with 1.

Track two values: the total number of steps needed to reach 1, and the maximum value that appears in the sequence (N counts too).

Example: N = 6 gives 6 3 10 5 16 8 4 2 1, which takes 8 steps, and the maximum value is 16. For N = 1 there are 0 steps and the maximum is 1.

Given N, print the sequence, the number of steps and the maximum value.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one positive integer N.
questions.output_format:
Three lines:
Line 1: Sequence: <n1> <n2> ... 1 (space-separated)
Line 2: Steps: <number of steps>
Line 3: Max value: <largest value in the sequence>
hints: Keep three things: the current number, a steps counter, and the maximum so far.
Loop while n != 1: if n % 2 == 0 then n //= 2, else n = 3 * n + 1.
After each change, increase steps, append n to the sequence and update the maximum.
questions.reference_solution:
n = int(input())
seq = [n]
steps = 0
mx = n
while n != 1:
    if n % 2 == 0:
        n //= 2
    else:
        n = 3 * n + 1
    steps += 1
    seq.append(n)
    if n > mx:
        mx = n
print("Sequence: " + " ".join(map(str, seq)))
print(f"Steps: {steps}")
print(f"Max value: {mx}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one positive integer N.
extra_fields.output_format:
Three lines:
Line 1: Sequence: <n1> <n2> ... 1 (space-separated)
Line 2: Steps: <number of steps>
Line 3: Max value: <largest value in the sequence>

questions.title: Prime Factorization Formatter
questions.objective: Decompose N into prime factors and print in canonical form p1^k1 x p2^k2.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Every integer greater than 1 can be written as a product of prime numbers. Write N in this prime factorization form by following these steps.

Step 1: Find the prime factors by trial division. Start with p = 2 and keep dividing N by p while it divides evenly, counting how many times you divided (this count is the exponent). Then move to the next p. Stop when p * p is greater than the remaining N.
Step 2: If the remaining N is greater than 1 after the loop, it is itself a prime factor with exponent 1.
Step 3: Print the factors in canonical form:
• Primes in increasing order
• Each factor is written as p^k (the prime, then ^, then the exponent)
• If the exponent is 1, print only p (no ^1)
• Factors are joined with " x " (a space, the letter x, a space)
• N = 1 has no prime factors, so print 1

Example 1: 360 = 2 * 2 * 2 * 3 * 3 * 5, so the output is 2^3 x 3^2 x 5.
Example 2: 97 is a prime number, so the output is 97.
Example 3: 49 = 7 * 7, so the output is 7^2.

Given N, print its prime factorization.
questions.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
questions.output_format: One line: Factorization: <factors in canonical form>
hints: Use p = 2 and increase p by 1 while p * p <= n.
Inside, use an inner while loop: while n % p == 0, divide n by p and count the exponent.
After the loop, if n > 1 then n is a prime factor with exponent 1.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing one integer N.
extra_fields.output_format: One line: Factorization: <factors in canonical form>

questions.title: Bisection Number Search
questions.objective: Simulate binary search over interval answering HIGHER, LOWER, CORRECT inputs.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A guessing helper uses binary search to find a secret number between low and high. After each guess it is told whether the secret number is HIGHER, LOWER or CORRECT. In this problem, these answers are given in the input, one answer per line.

Follow these rules:
• Start with the interval [low, high]
• Each guess is the middle of the interval: mid = (low + high) // 2
• Print each guess as: Guess k: mid (k = 1, 2, 3, ...)
• After each guess, read one answer
• Answer CORRECT: stop, the secret number is mid
• Answer HIGHER: the secret is bigger than mid, so continue with [mid + 1, high]
• Answer LOWER: the secret is smaller than mid, so continue with [low, mid - 1]
• If the interval becomes empty (low > high) before CORRECT is read, the answers contradict each other. Print Inconsistent responses and stop.

Example: low = 1, high = 100 and answers HIGHER, HIGHER, CORRECT. The guesses are 50, 75 and 88, so the secret number is 88, found in 3 guesses.

Given low, high and the answers, print every guess and then the result.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers low and high.
Then one answer per line, each exactly HIGHER, LOWER or CORRECT. There are always enough answer lines to finish the search.
questions.output_format:
One line for every guess: Guess <k>: <mid>
Then, if CORRECT was read, two lines:
Found: <mid>
Guesses: <total number of guesses>
If the answers are inconsistent, one line: Inconsistent responses
hints: Use while low <= high and compute mid = (low + high) // 2 in every round.
Read one answer per guess with input().strip(), and update low or high accordingly.
A while-else helps: the else part runs only when the loop ends without break, which is exactly the inconsistent case.
questions.reference_solution:
low, high = map(int, input().split())
guesses = 0
while low <= high:
    mid = (low + high) // 2
    guesses += 1
    print(f"Guess {guesses}: {mid}")
    resp = input().strip()
    if resp == "CORRECT":
        print(f"Found: {mid}")
        print(f"Guesses: {guesses}")
        break
    elif resp == "HIGHER":
        low = mid + 1
    else:
        high = mid - 1
else:
    print("Inconsistent responses")

questions.title: Armstrong Numbers in Range
questions.objective: Identify all Armstrong numbers in range [A, B] where sum of d-th powers equals N.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: An Armstrong number (also called a narcissistic number) is a number that is equal to the sum of its digits, where each digit is raised to the power of the number of digits in the number.
• Let d be the number of digits of the number
• Raise every digit to the power d and add the results
• If the sum is equal to the number, it is an Armstrong number
• Every single-digit number is an Armstrong number

Example 1: 153 has d = 3 digits, and 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3 = 1 + 125 + 27 = 153. So 153 is an Armstrong number.
Example 2: 1634 has d = 4 digits, and 1^4 + 6^4 + 3^4 + 4^4 = 1 + 1296 + 81 + 256 = 1634. So 1634 is an Armstrong number.
Example 3: 100 has d = 3 digits, and 1^3 + 0^3 + 0^3 = 1, which is not 100. So 100 is not an Armstrong number.

Find all Armstrong numbers from A to B (both included). Use a loop over the range with an inner loop (or a digit-extraction loop) for each number. Print the Armstrong numbers in increasing order on one line, separated by single spaces. If there is none, print a message saying so.
questions.input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers A and B.
questions.output_format:
If found, one line: Armstrong numbers: <n1> <n2> ... (space-separated, ascending)
If none, one line: No Armstrong numbers found
hints: First find d, the number of digits of the current number (for example with len(str(num)) or a loop).
Then sum digit ** d for every digit and compare the sum with the number.
Collect the matching numbers in a list and print them joined by spaces.
